requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 template variable IS a variable that stores templates.
requirements.original: A TTCN-3 template variable stores templates.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable-declaration
requirements.canonical: A template variable declaration IS the `var template` keywords followed by a type identifier and a variable identifier.
requirements.original: They are declared by the `var template` keyword followed by a type identifier and a variable identifier.

improper_terms.proper: `var` keyword followed by a template modifier (TemplateModifier)

ambiguity.issue: The prose speaks of a single 'var template keyword' and only a type identifier, while the syntactical structure uses `var` TemplateModifier (template, possibly with restriction) and TypeOrNestedTypeDef (which also allows a nested type definition or automatic typing).

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable-declaration
requirements.canonical: A template variable declaration MAY assign an initial content to the template variable.
requirements.original: An initial content can be assigned at declaration.

readings: A template variable declaration MAY assign an initial content to the template variable (the assignment is optional).
A template variable declaration SHALL assign an initial content, as the syntactical structure requires ":=" TemplateBody.
ambiguity.issue: The prose suggests an optional initial content, but the syntax block of 11.2 makes ":=" TemplateBody mandatory. The prose reading is kept in the canonical text; test authors should follow the syntax block.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.canonical: A template variable MAY store matching mechanisms in addition to values.
requirements.original: In addition to values, template variables may also store matching mechanisms (see clause 15.6.6).

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.canonical: A template variable MAY be used on the right hand side and on the left hand side of assignments.
requirements.original: Template variables may be used on the right hand side as well as on the left hand side of assignments, following the `return` keyword in bodies of functions defining a template-type return value in their headers and may be passed as actual parameters to template-type formal parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.canonical: A template variable MAY be used following the `return` keyword in the body of a function that defines a template-type return value in its header.
requirements.original: Template variables may be used on the right hand side as well as on the left hand side of assignments, following the `return` keyword in bodies of functions defining a template-type return value in their headers and may be passed as actual parameters to template-type formal parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.canonical: A template variable MAY be passed as actual parameter to a template-type formal parameter.
requirements.original: Template variables may be passed as actual parameters to template-type formal parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: A template instance MAY be assigned to a template variable or to a field of a template variable.
requirements.original: It is also allowed to assign a template instance to a template variable or a template variable field.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable-declaration
requirements.canonical: A template variable declaration has the syntax `var` TemplateModifier [ ( `@lazy` | `@fuzzy` ) [ `@deterministic` ] ] [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] followed by one or more comma-separated VarIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] ":=" TemplateBody and an optional ";".
requirements.original: var TemplateModifier [ (@lazy | @fuzzy) [ @deterministic ] ] [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] { VarIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] ":=" TemplateBody [ "," ] }+ [ ";" ]

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.canonical: A template variable IS an association of a name with the location of a template or a value.
requirements.original: A template variable associates a name with the location of a template or a value (as every value is also a template).

requirements.subject: ent:value
requirements.canonical: Every value IS also a template.
requirements.original: A template variable associates a name with the location of a template or a value (as every value is also a template).

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.canonical: A template variable MAY change its template several times during test execution.
requirements.original: A template variable may change its template during test execution several times.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.canonical: A template or value MAY be assigned several times to a template variable.
requirements.original: A template or value can be assigned several times to a template variable.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.canonical: A template variable MAY be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.original: The template variable can be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.

requirements.subject: ent:template-restriction
requirements.canonical: The content of a template variable MAY be restricted by a template restriction to the matching mechanisms specific value and `omit`, in the same way as formal template parameters.
requirements.original: The content of a template variable can be restricted to the matching mechanisms specific value and omit in the same way as formal template parameters, see clause 5.4.1.2.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-restriction
requirements.canonical: The template restriction `template (omit)` MAY be replaced by the shorthand notation `omit`.
requirements.original: The restriction template (omit) can be replaced by the shorthand notation omit.

requirements.subject: ent:template-concatenation
requirements.canonical: A string type template or a list type template CAN be concatenated.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: String and list type templates can be concatenated, see clause 15.11.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.canonical: A template variable SHALL NOT be declared or used in a module definitions part.
requirements.original: a) Template variables shall not be declared or used in a module definitions part (i.e. global variables are not supported in TTCN-3).

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.condition: the template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: A template variable used on the right hand side of an assignment SHALL NOT be an operand of a TTCN-3 operator.
requirements.original: b) When used on the right hand side of assignments template variables shall not be operands of TTCN-3 operators (see clause 7.1) and the variable on the left hand side shall be a template variable too.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.condition: the template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: If a template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment, the variable on the left hand side SHALL be a template variable.
requirements.original: b) When used on the right hand side of assignments template variables shall not be operands of TTCN-3 operators (see clause 7.1) and the variable on the left hand side shall be a template variable too.

readings: If a template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment, the variable on the left hand side SHALL be a template variable.

If a template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment, the target on the left hand side SHALL be a template variable or a field of a template variable (e.g. accessed via dot or index notation).
ambiguity.issue: 'the variable on the left hand side' does not say whether a field or element of a template variable counts; the second reading is consistent with 11.2-s006, the first is the literal reading and is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.condition: an element of a template variable is accessed in an assignment
requirements.canonical: When an element of a template variable is accessed on the left hand side or the right hand side of an assignment, the rules of clause 15.6 SHALL apply.
requirements.original: c) When accessing element of template variables either on the left hand side or on the right hand side of assignments, the rules given in clause 15.6 shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.canonical: The dot notation and the index notation MAY be used to inspect and modify fields of a template variable, although TTCN-3 operations SHALL NOT be applied directly to template variables.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: While it is not allowed to directly apply TTCN-3 operations to template variables, it is allowed to use the dot notation and the index notation to inspect and modify template variable fields.

ambiguity.issue: The NOTE says 'TTCN-3 operations' while restriction b) it explains speaks of 'TTCN-3 operators (see clause 7.1)'.

requirements.subject: ent:uninitialized-variable
requirements.canonical: Use of an uninitialized template variable at any place other than the left hand side of an assignment, a return statement, or an actual parameter passed to a formal parameter SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: d) Use of uninitialized template variables at other places than the left hand side of assignments, in return statements, or as actual parameters passed to formal parameters shall cause an error.

readings: Use of an uninitialized template variable in any other place SHALL cause an error (static or dynamic).
Use of an uninitialized template variable in any other place SHALL cause a dynamic error at runtime only.
ambiguity.issue: The kind of error (compile-time or runtime) is not stated; since template variable declarations require an initial TemplateBody, it is also unclear how a template variable can be uninitialized. The generic reading is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:template-restriction
requirements.condition: the template variable has a template restriction
requirements.canonical: If a template variable is restricted, the template used to initialize it SHALL contain only the matching mechanisms permitted by the restriction as described in clause 15.8.
requirements.original: f) If the template variable is restricted, then the template used to initialize it shall contain only the matching mechanisms as described in clause 15.8.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.condition: the template variable is used in a sending or receiving operation
requirements.canonical: A template variable SHALL be completely initialized in order to be used in a sending or receiving operation, as global and local templates.
requirements.original: g) Template variables, similarly to global and local templates, shall be fully specified in order to be used in sending and receiving operations.

ambiguity.issue: 'fully specified' is not a defined term; the glossary term 'completely initialized' is meant. For sending operations the template additionally has to resolve to a value (clause 15.0).

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable
requirements.canonical: The restrictions on templates given in clause 15.0 SHALL apply to template variables.
requirements.original: h) Restrictions on templates in clause 15.0 shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-variable
requirements.canonical: The initialization or assignment of a lazy or fuzzy template variable SHALL NOT contain a call of a function with `inout` or `out` parameters.
requirements.original: i) The initialization or assignment of a fuzzy or lazy variable shall not contain function calls of functions with inout or out parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function called in the initialization or assignment of a lazy or fuzzy template variable MAY internally call other functions with `inout` or `out` parameters.
requirements.original: The called functions may use other functions with inout or out parameters internally.

requirements.subject: ent:deterministic-modifier
requirements.condition: a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in a deterministic context
requirements.canonical: If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in a deterministic context (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or the initialization of a global non-fuzzy template), the variable SHALL be declared `@deterministic`.
requirements.original: j) If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic and the template body assigned to the variable shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.

requirements.subject: ent:template-body
requirements.condition: a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in a deterministic context
requirements.canonical: If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in a deterministic context, the template body assigned to the variable SHALL fulfil the restrictions on the content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.original: j) If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic and the template body assigned to the variable shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.

requirements.subject: ent:address-value
requirements.condition: the actual value of the address value is `null` (in the context of template variables)
requirements.canonical: Using the dot notation or the index notation to reference a field, alternative or element of an address value whose actual value is `null` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: k) Using the dot notation (see clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.2.1 and 6.2.5.1) and index notation (see clause 6.2.7) for referencing a field, alternative or element of an address value, which actual value is null shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:template-body
requirements.canonical: The template body on the right-hand side of the assignment symbol in a template variable declaration SHALL evaluate to a value or template that is type compatible with the declared template variable.
requirements.original: l) The template body at the right-hand side of the assignment symbol shall evaluate to a value or template, which is type compatible with the variable being declared.

requirements.subject: ent:template-body
requirements.canonical: The template body on the right-hand side of the assignment symbol in a template variable declaration SHALL evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.
requirements.original: m) The template body at the right-hand side of the assignment symbol shall evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable-declaration
requirements.canonical: If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a template variable declaration, the ArrayDef part SHALL be missing as well.
requirements.original: n) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" TemplateBody) shall be present.

requirements.subject: ent:template-variable-declaration
requirements.canonical: If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a template variable declaration, the assignment part (":=" TemplateBody) SHALL be present.
requirements.original: n) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" TemplateBody) shall be present.

requirements.subject: ent:fuzzy-variable
requirements.canonical: A fuzzy template variable IS evaluated on every usage.
requirements.original: var template @fuzzy float v_fuzzTemp1 := rnd(); // evaluated on every usage

non_requirement.reason: introduces the restrictions list of 11.2 and refers to the general static rules of clause 5
